title: Dynamic Customer Security Profile and On‑demand CAIQ Export
text:
Dynamic Customer Security Profile and On‑demand CAIQ Export

description:
Problem: Sales and Legal frequently ask for CAIQ exports and per-customer evidence sets during contract negotiations. The current process is manual: PM/solutions engineers bundle documents, redact where necessary, and hand off to customers. This creates multi-day delays, inconsistent answers, and an operational cost that scales linearly with enterprise deals.

Goal: Build a self-serve "Customer Security Profile" that compiles Redwood's canonical CAIQ answers, attached evidence, and a scoped export feature so customers (or our sales/legal teams) can generate a CAIQ or concise attestation tailored to the contract's scope. The feature should reduce manual effort, shorten procurement cycles, and surface usage-based pricing triggers when a customer indicates a high evidence burden.

Scope: UX in Console (Security > Attestations) and an API endpoint for on-demand export. Backend responsibilities include mapping internal answer sets to the CAIQ schema, evidence attachment catalog, redaction rules, RBAC for who can generate exports, audit logging for each export, and hooks to surface a pricing/credit recommendation to Pricing/RevOps when exports exceed thresholds.

acceptance_criteria:
Console: Customers and sales reps can generate a scoped CAIQ export for a selected product/region/date-range from the Customer Security Profile UI
API: /v1/customers/{id}/security-profile/export returns a CAIQ JSON file and a PDF summary with evidence reference links
Evidence minimization: Export applies configured heuristics to include only evidence relevant to the selected scope (configurable per-export)
RBAC & Audit: Exports are restricted to allowed roles and each export is recorded with user, timestamp, and export scope in audit logs
Redaction: PII or environment-specific secrets are automatically redacted using the approved redaction rules
Pricing signal: If an export or aggregated exports exceed configurable thresholds, a flag is emitted for Pricing to evaluate credits or contract adjustments

plan:
Phase 1 (Prototype): PRD + data model for mapping answers -> CAIQ, minimal Console mockup, security review of redaction rules
Phase 2 (Beta): Backend export service, API endpoint, attach evidence catalog, RBAC and audit events, internal beta with Sales & Legal
Phase 3 (Pilot): Customer pilot with two enterprise customers, measure time-to-sign and manual hours saved; iterate on heuristics
Phase 4 (Experiment): Run a pricing/credits experiment that surfaces an offer when a customer hits high evidence burden (track conversion)

comments:
2026-02-25 | Maya Chen: Initial PRD drafted. Included three UX patterns: full CAIQ export, scoped attestation summary, and automated 'evidence minimization' toggle. Requested ENG + SEC review for feasibility.
2026-03-02 | Derek Wallace: PM-Eng sync - ENG team estimates 4 sprints for core export plumbing (export format, RBAC, audit). Identified reusable pieces from ENG-90733. Requested sample CAIQ mappings from Security.
2026-03-05 | Priya Nair (Security): Reviewed redaction rules. Flag: MUSTNOT export raw customer logs or KMS keys. Proposed 'evidence references' pattern where artifacts are pointers not blobs in the export.
2026-03-07 | Design (Ana Rodriguez): Uploaded console mockups to Figma; UX includes 'Export history' table and 'Export scope' wizard. Action: provide edge-case flows for multi-region customers.
2026-03-09 | Sales (Jon Park): Two enterprise deals in pipeline requested ability to get a signed CAIQ PDF within 48 hours. Asked for a pilot with account-specific evidence attachments.
2026-03-12 | Derek Wallace: Scoped MVP agreed. Estimate 5 points. Security review requested before public beta. Next steps: ENG to open implementation PR and Sec to finalize redaction checklist.
